symptoms: Long narrow gray or tan lesions appear between the veins and can merge into large dead areas. The lower leaves are usually affected first.
cause: A fungal disease that survives on crop residues and spreads in warm, humid conditions.
cultural_control: Rotate away from maize, bury or remove infected residues where practical, and keep the field airy. Avoid planting maize after maize on the same land if possible.
chemical_option: Use only products registered in Uganda for maize leaf diseases if the outbreak is severe. Ask an agro-dealer or extension officer for the product and dose, wear protective clothing, and follow the label.
prevention: Use clean seed, rotate crops, and ask NARO or your extension officer for current recommended varieties.
see_officer_when: Seek local extension help if the disease moves to the upper leaves before the crop tassels.
source: Draft knowledge entry to verify against NARO, MAAIF, and FAO guidance.
